article.title: Joyagoo Size Guide: Measure Clothing and Shoes Before Buying
article.description: Choose clothing and shoe sizes on Joyagoo using seller charts, flat garment measurements and clear warehouse photo requests before international shipping.

facts.label: Compare with an item that already fits
Request the measurement that changes your decision

sections.heading: Choose a size from measurements, not the letter on the label
paragraphs: There is no single Joyagoo size chart that makes every seller's clothing and shoes equivalent. The useful chart belongs to the exact product and variation you are ordering. Start with a garment or pair of shoes that fits you well, record its measurements, and compare those measurements with the listing. A familiar label such as medium or EU 42 is a starting point, not evidence that two unrelated items have the same dimensions.

Make the comparison before paying, while another size or seller is still an easy option. Save the chart together with the product address, selected size and date. Listings can change, and a screenshot without the product identity is difficult to use later. If the seller supplies no measurements, ask the agent whether they can obtain them. Decide how much uncertainty you are comfortable accepting instead of treating an absent chart as permission to use your usual size.

sections.heading: Read the chart headings and measurement method
paragraphs: Check whether the figures describe the wearer's body or the finished garment. A chest circumference for a person is not the same as a shirt measured flat across the chest. A flat width of 56 cm corresponds to approximately 112 cm around that part of the garment, but doubling the number does not describe its stretch, shape or room for movement. Use the same measurement method on both the reference garment and the seller's chart.

Confirm centimetres versus inches before comparing numbers. One inch equals 2.54 centimetres; keep the original unit in your notes to avoid repeated rounding. Read any seller tolerance as a possible variation, not as a promise that the delivered item will hit the centre value. If the acceptable range is narrow, request clarification. A chart with several unexplained columns needs an explanation of each column, particularly shoulder width, sleeve length and measurements taken from different starting points.

sections.heading: Build a clothing reference that you can reuse
paragraphs: Lay a well-fitting garment flat without stretching it. For a top, record chest width from side to side, body length using a stated starting point, shoulder width if the seams are comparable, and sleeve length. Photograph the tape position so you can repeat the method. A dropped shoulder or curved hem makes a number less useful unless you also describe where the measurement begins and ends. Choose a reference with a similar cut and fabric to the item you want.

For trousers, note the waist measured flat, rise, thigh width and inseam. Separate a relaxed elastic waist from a stretched measurement. A waistband that can expand does not guarantee comfortable room through the hips or thighs. If the reference fits only with a belt or feels restrictive when sitting, record that too. The purpose is to describe a fit you actually want, rather than to collect numbers that look precise but come from an unsuitable comparison item.

sections.heading: Compare fit, fabric and layering before choosing between sizes
paragraphs: Two products with similar measurements can feel different because of fabric, lining and construction. A rigid jacket needs a different fit decision from a stretchy base layer. Decide whether you plan to wear a shirt, a thick sweater or nothing bulky underneath. Compare the seller's measurements with your reference while accounting for that intended use. Avoid a universal instruction to size up: increasing one dimension can also make sleeves, shoulders or the overall length unsuitable.

Consider this illustrative comparison. Your reference shirt measures 55 cm across the chest and 72 cm in body length. A listing offers one size at 54 by 71 cm and another at 57 by 74 cm. Neither is automatically correct. The first may feel tighter, while the second may be longer than you want. Check the remaining dimensions, the seller's tolerance and your preferred fit. If neither option meets the important measurements, a different cut can be a better choice than compromising on every dimension.

sections.heading: Check shoe sizing with the seller’s own definitions
paragraphs: Record the size system used by the listing and whether it distinguishes men's, women's or children's shoes. US, UK, EU and centimetre labels should not be converted through a random universal table. Prefer the seller's chart for that product and ask what any centimetre figure describes. Foot length, insole length and outsole length are different measurements. An outsole photograph cannot tell you the space available inside the shoe, especially around a tapered toe or thick heel padding.

Measure both feet using the same method and record the larger result, then follow the chart's instructions for how that measurement is used. Do not add a fixed allowance unless the seller explains that it is required. If requesting an insole measurement at the warehouse, ask whether the insole can be removed without damage and how it will be measured. Compare it with a similar well-fitting shoe, while recognising that width, toe shape and internal volume still affect comfort.

sections.heading: Use warehouse photos to check the specific order
paragraphs: When QC photographs become available, first match them with the product order and selected variation. Check the size label, colour and quantity before spending time on a detailed measurement. A correctly labelled size may still differ from the listing's measurements, and a photographed label is not a fit test. If one dimension would change your decision, ask for a clear photograph showing the complete tape, its starting point and the relevant garment or shoe in the same frame.

Make the request specific. For example, ask for the shirt laid flat with the tape running horizontally between the underarm seams, without stretching the fabric. For trousers, specify whether you need relaxed waist width or inseam. Avoid asking simply for a better photo when the real problem is an undefined measuring method. Confirm the availability and price of additional services in the account, then check any return deadline while you wait. An unanswered measurement request should not be assumed to pause that deadline.

sections.heading: Decide whether to keep, clarify or request a return
paragraphs: Put the ordered specification, seller chart and warehouse evidence next to one another. Separate a visible mismatch, such as the wrong size label, from a preference issue, such as wanting a looser fit than the chart suggested. Keep a short explanation of the problem and attach the relevant photographs to the existing order discussion. This helps the agent understand whether you need a corrected measurement, a seller response or information about the available after-sales options.

Do not remove labels or request disposal of retail packaging while a return decision remains open. Check the current conditions and costs before accepting an exchange, especially if a replacement would arrive after the rest of your parcel is ready. If the evidence is insufficient and the deadline is close, ask for a clear next step rather than waiting indefinitely. A decision made before international packing generally leaves more practical options than discovering a sizing concern after the parcel has been dispatched.

sections.heading: Keep a small size record for your next order
paragraphs: Save the final measurements, the size you received and a brief note about fit once the item arrives. Include the seller or product identifier because a successful size from one listing does not establish a rule for every other listing. Record whether the measurement was taken before or after washing, since comparing different conditions can be misleading. Over time, a few reliable reference items are more useful than a long list of unexplained size labels copied from other buyers.

Before submitting your next parcel, check that each item has an acceptance decision and that every unresolved measurement has a named follow-up. Use the general QC checklist for quantity and visible condition, and the shoe QC guide for pair-specific checks. Browse the spreadsheet by product name or source ID only after you know which measurements matter. Product discovery finds candidates; the size comparison determines whether a candidate is suitable for you.

article.title: Joyagoo Link Not Working? Check Product IDs and Listings
article.description: Troubleshoot a Joyagoo product link, distinguish a deleted listing from a loading problem, and use source IDs or image search to check alternatives.

facts.label: Do not confuse it with a catalogue page number
A working link does not prove stock availability
Similar photos may belong to different products

sections.heading: Identify which part of the product link has failed
paragraphs: A Joyagoo link that does not work can describe several different problems: the spreadsheet page is unavailable, the original marketplace listing has disappeared, the Joyagoo product page cannot load, or the desired variation is no longer offered. Start by identifying which page failed and what message it displays. Save the full address and product identifier before trying alternatives. Repeatedly opening different converters without preserving the original listing can make it harder to establish which item you intended to buy.

Keep three records separate: the catalogue page used to discover the product, the original seller listing, and the page used to place the order through Joyagoo. They serve different purposes and may use different identifiers. A catalogue card can remain visible after the seller changes stock, while a live seller page can temporarily fail to load through an agent. Your first goal is to locate the break between those stages, not to assume that every loading error means the product has been deleted.

sections.heading: Copy a complete product address and preserve its identifier
paragraphs: Use the original product link where possible. When copying from a spreadsheet or chat message, check that the address has not been cut off at punctuation or mixed with surrounding text. Do not remove parameters blindly: one of them may identify the product or selected option. Open the address in a normal browser tab and compare the title, seller and images with your saved reference. If a short link redirects, record the final listing address as well as the shared version.

On this site, a catalogue route number and the source marketplace product ID are different values. The product detail page shows the source ID, and its Joyagoo button uses that value for the purchase handoff. Do not take the number from the end of a local catalogue URL and paste it into another platform's product parameter. Keep the marketplace name beside the identifier because a numeric ID alone does not explain which platform owns the listing.

sections.heading: Check the original listing before blaming the agent page
paragraphs: Look for the original seller page and inspect the specific option you wanted. A listing may still exist while a particular colour, size or configuration is unavailable. The visible headline price may refer to another option, so compare the selected variation as well as the title. If the seller page says the item was removed, save that message. A copied spreadsheet entry or an old QC image does not restore a deleted listing or establish that its former seller can still supply it.

If the marketplace requires a session or displays a regional access screen, treat that as an access limitation rather than proof of deletion. Ask the agent to check availability using the original link and exact variation. Avoid paying for a vaguely similar replacement just to move the order forward. Before accepting an alternative, confirm what changed in the seller, specification, quantity and price. A successful page load is useful evidence of access, but it is not a stock reservation.

sections.heading: Separate a temporary loading problem from a purchase problem
paragraphs: If the seller listing is available but Joyagoo does not display the product, record the time and the exact error. Try the complete original address in the product search field and check whether the returned title and options match. If the site reports a temporary service problem, retry later instead of creating several paid orders. Keep any existing order identifier visible so that a second attempt does not accidentally become a duplicate purchase of the same item.

A different browser session can help distinguish a stale page from an ongoing service issue, but it should not become a way to bypass a restriction. Do not share passwords or payment details with a converter, a spreadsheet operator or someone offering to repair the link. The information normally useful for an agent investigation is the product address, source ID, requested variation, screenshot and time. If the order has already been paid, use its existing message thread so the agent can see the transaction context.

sections.heading: Search the spreadsheet with a product name or source ID
paragraphs: The catalogue on this site supports text searches, including source product identifiers. Start with the ID when you have it, then try a short descriptive name if no result appears. A brand or broad category can return many unrelated items, so use details such as garment type or a distinctive model name to narrow the comparison. Search results are discovery aids rather than a confirmation that a seller currently has your chosen size available for immediate purchase.

Open each candidate's detail page and compare the source ID, images, variation and available price information. A matching photograph with a different identifier may represent another seller, a relisted item or a different product entirely. Do not quietly substitute it into an order that was approved for another listing. Keep a note explaining why the alternative is suitable and which details still need confirmation. If the exact source ID produces no result, it may simply be absent from this catalogue; that alone does not establish that it is unavailable everywhere.

sections.heading: Use image search to find candidates, then verify the details
paragraphs: Image search is useful when a saved product photograph is the only reference you have. Choose a clear image with the item prominent and as little background clutter as possible. On this site's image-search page, visual comparison runs on your device against the catalogue index. Results indicate visual similarity, not seller identity, authenticity or an exact product match. A similar silhouette or colour arrangement can produce a promising result that still needs a careful listing comparison.

After opening a result, compare details that distinguish the item: material description, dimensions, closure type, pattern placement, included accessories and the selected variation. Check the source ID rather than relying on the thumbnail. If several sellers reuse the same studio photograph, the photo cannot establish which one made or holds the item. Request information through the normal order process before paying. Image search is most effective as a way to rebuild a shortlist, followed by the same size and QC checks you would apply to any other purchase.

sections.heading: Ask the agent about a manual order when normal search fails
paragraphs: Joyagoo's shopping guidance describes a manual ordering option for products that cannot be found through ordinary search. Check whether that option is available in your account and what information it requires. Provide the original link, seller details, variation, quantity and a clear reference image. Explain the loading problem without asserting that a particular service will support every marketplace or every product. The agent needs to confirm whether the request can be fulfilled under the current conditions.

Before approving payment, review the specification and any additional costs attached to the request. Make sure the recorded product is the one you intended, especially when a seller communicates through an album or a message rather than a conventional listing. Ask how availability and after-sales conditions will be confirmed. A manual order can be an alternative workflow, but it does not eliminate the need to verify size, seller information, restrictions or the evidence you will want when the item reaches the warehouse.

sections.heading: Save the repaired link and close the loop
paragraphs: Once you have a usable listing, save the final source address, source ID and selected variation together. If you discovered the item through an outdated spreadsheet entry, keep the old address in your notes so you can recognise the change later. Record whether the problem was a broken catalogue link, a removed seller listing, unavailable stock or a temporary loading failure. That short explanation prevents you from repeating the same investigation when you revisit the product or share it with someone else.

If you already have a paid order, confirm its status before purchasing from the repaired link. Ask the agent whether the original order should continue, change or be cancelled, and wait for the relevant confirmation. Then move to the size guide and QC checklist rather than treating link recovery as the end of the buying decision. The useful outcome is a traceable product and an accurate order, with enough information to decide whether to keep the item before international shipping.

article.title: Joyagoo Shoe QC Checklist: Sizes, Pairs, Soles and Photos
article.description: Inspect Joyagoo shoe QC photos for matching pairs, size labels, visible damage and missing angles, then decide what to clarify before shipping.

facts.label: Match size labels and the ordered variation
Keep packaging while after-sales questions remain

sections.heading: Match the photographs to the shoes you actually ordered
paragraphs: A useful Joyagoo shoe QC review starts with order identity, not a judgement about how attractive the pair looks. Open the paid order and compare the selected model, colour, size and quantity with the warehouse photographs. Check that the images show both shoes from that order. Seller studio photographs and images from another buyer can help you understand a design, but they do not show the condition of the pair currently waiting for your acceptance decision.

Keep the product link, variation and order identifier beside the photos. If a detail seems inconsistent, describe the difference in those terms rather than saying only that the shoes look wrong. A box label is helpful, but it should not replace the labels or markings on the shoes themselves. Packaging can be mismatched. Check the item first, then the packaging and accessories, and record any missing evidence before deciding whether the pair is ready to join your international parcel.

sections.heading: Check size labels on both shoes and understand their limits
paragraphs: Look for a readable size label on each shoe and compare them with one another and with the ordered size system. A correct label confirms part of the specification; it does not prove that the shoe will fit. Different shapes, widths, linings and toe boxes can make shoes with the same nominal size feel different. Use the dedicated size guide to compare the seller's chart with a suitable reference pair rather than converting every label through one generic size table.

If an internal measurement is important, ask whether the warehouse can provide it safely and what method they will use. An insole measurement, an outsole measurement and your foot length are not interchangeable. Request a photograph with the start and end of the tape visible and avoid instructions that require damaging a fixed insole. If the measurement remains uncertain, record that uncertainty explicitly. A long-looking outsole in a photograph should not be used to overrule a conflicting size label or a clearly unsuitable seller chart.

sections.heading: Compare the pair from matching angles
paragraphs: Ask for views that let you compare the left and right shoe under similar conditions. A top view can reveal differences in lacing, tongue position or overall shape. Front and rear views help you compare toe areas and heel alignment. Side views show panels and sole joins, while an outsole view shows the underside. You do not need every conceivable photograph; choose the angles that would actually resolve a concern about your pair or its ordered specification.

Perspective matters. A shoe closer to the camera can look larger, and one tilted heel can appear uneven even when the pair is aligned normally. Before calling an apparent difference a defect, ask for a level comparison on the same surface if that would settle the question. Keep your request specific about the angle and feature. A repeated wide shot from the same position adds little when the uncertainty concerns a small seam, a label or the edge of a sole.

sections.heading: Inspect visible condition without promising performance
paragraphs: Review the upper, lining where visible, stitching, fasteners and the join between upper and sole. Look for visible tears, stains, missing parts, unusual gaps or a mismatch between the two shoes. Distinguish a feature of the design from damage by checking the listing reference. If a mark may be lighting or dust, request a close-up before deciding. Photographs can document a visible concern; they cannot determine every material property or how the shoes will perform after repeated wear.

Do not describe a pair as authenticated, durable, waterproof or comfortable simply because its QC pictures look acceptable. A warehouse photograph is not a material test or a long-term wear test. Likewise, a photograph cannot establish smell or accurately reproduce every colour on every screen. Note what is visible and what remains unknown. This keeps the decision useful: you can accept the observed condition while still recognising the limits of the evidence, or ask for a particular check when the service is available.

sections.heading: Check soles, closures and included accessories
paragraphs: Inspect the outsole pattern, edges and any visible mismatch between the pair. Check that both shoes have the expected laces, straps, buckles or other closures. If the listing includes extra laces, insoles, tags or another accessory, confirm the agreed contents against the order rather than assuming that every studio photograph shows what is included. Keep a short contents list so that a missing accessory can be explained clearly while the item is still at the warehouse.

Consider this hypothetical case: the pair appears correct from above, but the listing includes a second set of laces and only one set appears in the photographs. The next action is to ask whether the additional laces are inside the box, not to reject the shoes immediately or assume the accessory is present. If the box is needed for that check, postpone its removal. Review the answer and any supporting photograph before closing the concern or making the packing instructions final.

sections.heading: Write a photo request that leads to a decision
paragraphs: A strong request identifies the order, the concern and the evidence needed. For example, ask for a close-up of the outer sole join on the right shoe because the existing image appears to show a gap. Or request both heel counters photographed level from the back because the current angle makes alignment unclear. Avoid asking for a complete new photo set when one focused image would answer the question. Keep the original photograph so the agent can locate the area quickly.

Check whether additional photographs or measurements are available and whether there is a charge before ordering the service. Read the return or exchange deadline on the same day. Do not assume that requesting another image extends the time available for after-sales action. If the evidence is still incomplete near the deadline, ask the agent what options remain. Maintain one clear discussion on the existing order rather than scattering different instructions across several channels that may not share the same context.

sections.heading: Make an acceptance decision before changing the packaging
paragraphs: Use three practical outcomes for your review: accept the visible condition, request clarification, or ask about the available return or exchange process. A clarification should name the missing information and how it could change your decision. A return request should identify the mismatch or concern and include the relevant evidence. Read the seller and agent conditions rather than assuming that every concern qualifies for a free return or that every cost will be refunded.

Keep the shoes, labels and packaging intact while the decision is open. Removing a box can reduce parcel volume, but it is a separate packing choice with consequences for protection and after-sales handling. Once you accept the pair, review the shoebox guide to compare packaging options against the selected shipping line's measurements and conditions. Do not ask for box removal only because someone else's parcel was cheaper; your contents, destination and actual packed dimensions determine the useful comparison.

sections.heading: Keep the evidence through dispatch and delivery
paragraphs: Save the accepted QC images, the order specification and the final packing instructions with the parcel identifier. When several pairs are consolidated, record which orders belong to the parcel so that later tracking or delivery questions can be matched to the correct contents. Check the parcel record for the selected service and any requested protection. An item being stored is not the same as a parcel being dispatched, so keep those events separate in your notes.

When the parcel arrives, compare the received contents with the saved record and document any visible problem before discarding packaging. Contact the relevant service through its current process if something needs investigation. Use the experience to improve your next request: perhaps a size label, accessory photo or clearer heel view would have helped. The aim of this checklist is a timely, evidence-based purchase decision. It complements the general QC guide without turning a set of photographs into a guarantee about authenticity, fit or future performance.

joyagoo-return-window-warehouse-storage.description: Check Joyagoo return timing, keep QC evidence, request a refund through the order and distinguish return eligibility from warehouse storage.

section.heading: Check the return deadline before planning storage
paragraphs: A storage allowance is not a return allowance. Joyagoo’s shopping guidance describes a return or exchange request period after QC, while storage is a separate warehouse service. Read the deadline and available return control on your actual order as soon as the photographs arrive. Save the selected variation, QC images and the reason for the request. Do not wait for the rest of a haul before reviewing an item that may need to go back.

To start a refund enquiry, open the relevant order, check the return or exchange option and send a specific explanation with evidence. Confirm seller acceptance, return transport costs and the destination of any refund before treating the request as complete. Keep packaging and labels while the decision is open. If the deadline or control is unclear, ask the agent through that same order; additional photo requests and storage extensions should not be assumed to extend return eligibility.

joyagoo-qc-photo-checklist.seoTitle: Joyagoo QC Photos: What to Check Before Shipping
joyagoo-qc-photo-checklist.title: Joyagoo QC Photos: What to Check Before Shipping
joyagoo-qc-photo-checklist.description: Review Joyagoo QC photos for the right item, size, quantity and visible damage. Learn which extra photos to request before accepting your order.

section.heading: Use QC photos to make a keep-or-clarify decision
paragraphs: Start with the order number, selected variation and quantity, then compare the photographs with what you paid for. Check readable size labels, the main front and back views, visible damage and any included accessories. If a measurement determines whether the item is suitable, request that measurement with a clear starting point. General product photographs in a spreadsheet may help discovery, but the acceptance decision needs evidence attached to your own warehouse order.

Separate visible findings from unknowns. Photos do not establish fit, authenticity or long-term performance. A missing angle is a reason for a focused request, not a reason to assume the hidden area is satisfactory. For shoes, use the pair-specific checklist; for clothing, compare the seller chart and your reference garment. Check the return deadline while waiting for extra evidence and make the decision before removing labels, discarding packaging or submitting the item for international shipping.

joyagoo-fees-explained.seoTitle: Joyagoo Fees Explained: Product, Shipping and Extra Costs
joyagoo-fees-explained.title: Joyagoo Fees Explained: Product, Shipping and Extra Costs
joyagoo-fees-explained.description: Understand Joyagoo costs from the seller price and domestic delivery to international shipping, optional services and payment conversion.

section.heading: Build a complete cost record before comparing totals
paragraphs: Separate the product price, seller-to-warehouse delivery, international shipping and optional services in your notes. Then record payment or currency-conversion costs actually shown during checkout. A cheap listing price does not tell you the delivered total, and a shipping estimate made before packing is not the final measured parcel charge. Compare quotes only when the destination, selected contents, packaging and service conditions match.

Keep a dated quote beside the payment receipt and distinguish an estimate, a paid deposit and a later adjustment. Confirm which extras you selected and why each one is useful. For example, an additional shoe measurement addresses a fit uncertainty, while protective packing addresses a transport concern; they are separate decisions. Review the current checkout and route terms for applicable charges rather than relying on a universal cost per kilogram or an old coupon claim.

joyagoo-order-status-stock-arrived-qc-st.seoTitle: Joyagoo Stock Arrived Meaning: Order Status and Next Steps
joyagoo-order-status-stock-arrived-qc-st.title: Joyagoo Stock Arrived Meaning: Order Status and Next Steps
joyagoo-order-status-stock-arrived-qc-st.description: Stock Arrived means warehouse receipt before QC and storage. See what to check next and how order progress differs from international parcel shipping.

section.heading: Stock Arrived is a warehouse stage, not international dispatch
paragraphs: Joyagoo’s official status guide describes Stock Arrived as awaiting quality checking and storage. Open the individual order to check its variation and whether photographs are available. Review the images when they appear, request any decision-critical measurement and check the after-sales deadline. QC Completed and Stored in Warehouse describe later warehouse steps; neither label alone proves that an international parcel has departed.

If you are looking for delivery progress, open the separate parcel record and confirm that the accepted items were submitted, the required payment was completed and a dispatch event was recorded. Keep the product order number and parcel number separate. For a missing product page, check the source link before placing another order; for missing QC pictures, use the photo troubleshooting guide. This avoids turning an unclear status into an unnecessary duplicate purchase.
